text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.
-A report from Norwegian shipbroker Fearnleys says there is now less uncertainty in Norway's shipping business. In 1996, shipping companies ordered new ships worth 17 billion crowns.

-Norwegian macro-economic experts expect the central bank to cut interest rates soon. A recent cut in interest rates has not succeeded in weakening the crown. Last year the crown's value rose by three percent versus the inverse ECU index.

-Norwegian industrial group Norsk Hydro has had little success with its fertilizer business in Guatemala. However, the company expects cooperation with competitor Ux SA will improve results considerably.
-Norwegian companies spend more on advertising than ever before. Norway's largest advertising company, Leo Burnett, posted about 82 million crowns in income last year, up 30 percent from 1995.

-A decision by Scandinavian Airlines Systems to cut commission to travel agencies could result in losses for the airliner, because travel agents say they will try to avoid selling SAS tickets to passengers.
